name: Cyrus
description: Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return

points: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: Cyrus declares that the Lord God of heaven has given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and calls any of the Lord's people to go up, showing again that the Most High sets over the earth one that is profitable for his purpose.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: In the first year of Cyrus the word of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah is fulfilled. The Lord stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout his kingdom.
Cyrus was one of the first kings of Persia, and the Most High used him to give the order to rebuild Jerusalem. His coming was prophesied long before by name.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

points: During the Persian captivity, we got liberty. The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth: he said that because he knew it was a prophecy. It goes into more detail when you read the writings of Flavius Josephus, on how the prophets were showing Cyrus what he must do. And he obeyed that.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia the Lord stirred up his spirit to proclaim that the Lord God of heaven had given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him an house at Jerusalem. The Persians ruled the whole earth at one point, and Cyrus let Israel go up out of the seventy years in Babylon to rebuild the temple. To understand why Iran was attacked you have to know who the Persians are today.

note.label: The Real Reason Iran Was Attacked

points: The Achaemenid Empire, founded by Cyrus the Great in 550 BC, was an ancient Iranian empire. The Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, and he proclaimed that the God of heaven had charged him to build him a house at Jerusalem.
Cyrus brings out the vessels of the house of the Lord that Nebuchadnezzar had carried from Jerusalem and stored among his own goods.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

points: They give money to the masons and carpenters, and meat, drink, and oil to the men of Zidon and Tyre to bring cedars from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa, according to the grant of Cyrus.

note.label: Ezra 3: The Foundation of the Temple Is Laid

points: Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us. Right? The same way we were told to build it, that is the way we are going to build it. So we must separate. We must separate.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: Israel would build to the Lord alone as Cyrus commanded. The forefathers understood that the work of the Most High is not shared with other nations.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

points: They hire counselors to frustrate the purpose all the days of Cyrus, even until the reign of Darius, a hindrance stretching across the kings in between.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

points: Cyrus is called king of Babylon because he conquered Babylon and took possession of all it held, though he reigned out of Persia. He restored the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: The letter asks Darius to search the king's treasure house to confirm that Cyrus made a decree to build the house of God at Jerusalem. The heathen always keep records on the children of Israel, so the matter had to be proven from the rolls.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: The decree ordered the house rebuilt with strong foundations and set dimensions, the expenses given out of the king's house, and the gold and silver vessels restored to their place. Cyrus helped fund the rebuilding of the house of Israel.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: The elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo; and they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

That saith to Jerusalem, thou shalt be inhabited, and to the cities of Judah, ye shall be built, raising up the decayed places. That saith of Cyrus, he is my shepherd and shall perform all my pleasure, saying to Jerusalem thou shalt be built and to the temple thy foundation shall be laid. Jerusalem will be the place where Christ's feet touch down and Israel rules the world, not the gentiles trodding it down now.

note.label: Isaiah 44: The Idol Maker's Folly and the Changed Name

points: Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him and loose the loins of kings, to open the two-leaved gates that shall not be shut.

note.label: Isaiah 45: I Form the Light and Create Darkness

points: So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian. He had a wise and humble spirit, was beloved by the king, could answer visions and interpret dreams, and was of the king's seed as shown in chapter one.

note.label: Daniel 6: Daniel in the Den of Lions

points: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a thing was revealed unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar, and the thing was true but the time appointed was long, and he understood the vision.

note.label: Daniel 10: A Man Clothed in Linen
